safety_review.findings: Fresh review by a non-author of every reply in all 13 banks, every option, all 3 alternatives, Thai and English, read against every question variant of its bank. Sources opened: WHO, The treatment of diarrhoea, a manual for physicians and other senior health workers, 4th revision (2005), cached text (Table 1 grading, skin pinch caveats, Plans A and B incl. vomiting wait 5-10 min, 50-100 mL per stool under 2 years, repeat Plan B with food, zinc 10-14 days and recurrence benefit, NG or IV Ringer's lactate when ORT fails, hypernatraemia from too concentrated drinks, antiemetics); WHO guideline on management of pneumonia and diarrhoea in children up to 10 years of age (2024), recommendations 1a-3c. The Thai 2019 paediatric acute diarrhoea guideline was not opened in this review; Thai-guidance claims (electrolytes mainly for severe or atypical cases, ondansetron allowed) were checked against the case's own safety review. Confirmed the earlier fixes: step2.B/W urineout[1] weigh, step5.W restartb[0] strength, ondansetron named in step3.B/R ondan[2] and step4.W ondan[1] weigh, glucose Thai fingerprick bold, electrolyte weigh lines credit Thai guidance. No must-fix: no wrong fact or dose, no reassurance of a harmful action, no delay of needed treatment, no ranking or later-step preview, no out-of-option drug, test or treatment named. Non-blocking notes: zinc benefit statements follow WHO, while the Thai guideline limits zinc (already on #470); WHO 2005 says antiemetics should never be given (older sedating drugs), which the ondansetron weigh softens to local practice varies; Thai/English nuance gaps that do not change meaning: step3 planb/clinic[1] weigh (Thai several more days vs well over a week), step1 intus[2] weigh (Thai states the signs are absent vs none is described), step3 iv[2] weigh (English example absent in Thai), step2 elec[1] weigh (thirsty vs dehydrated), step2 assess[1] strength (free absent in Thai); step4.R spoon th[0] strength reads slightly awkwardly.
